title: 第十四章梦狼第十三章鬼母第十二章王成
lines: 第十四章梦狼
宋焘看完《鬼母》，在窗前坐了很久。他想那个母亲，想她穿墙而过的背影，想她说“我放心了”。他想起自己的母亲，想起她临终前的眼神，想起她说“你要好好活着”。他想了很久，想到月亮升起来，又落下去，才闭上眼睛，沉沉睡去。
第二天醒来，他翻开天书。书页自己翻动，停在一页空白上。他等着，等字迹浮现。
这一章，叫《梦狼》。
河北有个老翁，姓白，名世昌，做过一任县丞，年老归乡，在家读书教子，安度晚年。他有两个儿子，大儿子白甲，二儿子白乙。白甲做了官，在江南某县当县令；白乙在家读书，侍奉老父。
白世昌平生最恨贪官。他做县丞的时候，清廉自守，从不收受贿赂，离任时老百姓送了他一把万民伞，他当宝贝一样供在堂屋里，每天上香。他常对两个儿子说：“做官如做人，要堂堂正正，清清白白。宁可穷死，不能贪死。”
白甲听了这话，嘴上答应，心里不以为然。他觉得父亲太迂腐，都什么年代了，还讲那一套。做官不捞钱，那做官做什么？他上任之后，明面上清廉公正，暗地里贪赃枉法，收受贿赂，草菅人命。谁送的钱多，谁就有理；谁不送钱，谁就没理。百姓恨之入骨，但他手腕高明，上司打点得好，一直稳稳地坐在位子上。
白世昌不知道这些。他只看见儿子每年寄回来的银子越来越多，信里说朝廷加了俸禄，上司赏识他，百姓爱戴他。白世昌信以为真，逢人便夸：“我儿子有出息，比我强多了。”
这一年冬天，白世昌做了一个梦。梦里他走在一条大路上，走着走着，忽然看见路边有一群人，穿着破衣烂衫，蓬头垢面，被差役押着往前走。那些人走得很慢，一步一挪，像是脚上戴着镣铐。白世昌凑近一看，认出其中几个是他老家的人，有邻居，有亲戚，还有他小时候的玩伴。
他吃了一惊，拉住一个差役问：“这些人犯了什么罪？”
差役看了他一眼，说：“他们都是被你儿子害的。”
白世昌的脸白了。“我儿子？哪个儿子？”
“白甲。”差役说，“他在江南做官，贪赃枉法，鱼肉百姓。这些人都是他的治下之民，被他逼得家破人亡，流落至此。”
白世昌浑身发抖，他不敢相信。他拉住那个差役，想再问清楚，差役甩开他的手，说：“你自己去看吧。前面就是他的衙门。”
白世昌顺着大路往前走，走了一段，看见一座衙门。衙门口蹲着两只石狮子，张着大嘴，露出锋利的牙齿。他正要进去，忽然从门里窜出一只狼。
那狼通体灰白，眼睛血红，嘴里叼着一只人手，正在嚼。它看见白世昌，停下来，歪着头看他。白世昌吓得腿都软了，往后退了几步。那狼没有扑上来，只是盯着他看，看了很久，然后转身，慢悠悠地走回了衙门。
白世昌站在门口，犹豫了很久。他想进去看看，但又怕那只狼。最后他还是迈步走了进去。
衙门里阴森森的，光线昏暗，地上到处是血。他沿着走廊往前走，走到大堂前，推开门，看见里面坐着一个人——不，不是人，是一只狼。那只狼穿着官服，戴着乌纱帽，坐在太师椅上，面前摆着案卷，正在审案。它的爪子握着朱笔，在案卷上勾勾画画。旁边站着两个狼衙役，手里拿着水火棍，面目狰狞。
白世昌看着那只狼，忽然觉得它的眉眼有些眼熟。他仔细一看，浑身一震——那狼的眉目，竟和他儿子白甲一模一样。
“甲儿？”他的声音在发抖。
那只狼抬起头，看了他一眼。它的眼睛是红的，但红里有一丝黑，黑里有一丝白，白里有一丝……他认不出的东西。那东西像是人性，又像是鬼性，像是他儿子，又像不是。
“爹，”那只狼开口了，声音和白甲一模一样，“你怎么来了？”
白世昌的眼泪唰地流了下来。他指着那只狼，手指在发抖。“你……你怎么变成这个样子了？”
白甲低头看了看自己的爪子，笑了笑。那笑和从前一样，嘴角弯弯的，但露出来的牙齿是尖的。
“爹，做官就是这样。你不吃人，人就要吃你。我也是没办法。”
白世昌气得浑身发抖，指着白甲的鼻子骂：“我从小是怎么教你的？堂堂正正做人，清清白白做官！你都忘了吗？”
白甲没有说话。它低下头，看着桌上的案卷，沉默了很久。然后它抬起头，看着白世昌，眼睛里的红淡了一些，黑多了一些。
“爹，你说的那些，我都记得。但我做不到。这个世道，清官做不下去。你不贪，别人贪；你清廉，别人害你。我不想害人，但我不想被人害。”
白世昌看着它，心里又疼又恨。他想起小时候的白甲，白白胖胖的，喜欢趴在他膝盖上听故事。他讲包公，讲海瑞，讲那些清官的故事。白甲听得很认真，听完说：“爹，我长大了也要做清官。”他笑了，说：“好，爹等着。”
他等到了。等来的，是一只狼。
他转身，走了。走出衙门，走出大路，走出那个梦。他醒来的时候，枕头湿了一片，全是泪。
白世昌病了。他躺在床上，不吃不喝，只是发呆。白乙守在床前，问他怎么了，他不说。问他是不是不舒服，他摇头。问他梦见什么了，他的眼泪又流了下来。
白乙慌了，赶紧去请郎中。郎中来看了，说老翁身体没什么大毛病，是心病。白乙问什么心病，郎中说不知道。
白世昌躺了三天，第四天挣扎着起来，让白乙备纸笔。白乙给他拿来，他写了一封信，写给白甲。信里说了那个梦，说梦见你变成了一只狼，说你贪赃枉法，鱼肉百姓。他说你赶紧改，赶紧把贪的银子退回去，赶紧做个好人。你要是不改，我就没有你这个儿子。
白乙把信送了出去。过了两个月，白甲的回信来了。信写得很客气，说爹你放心，儿子清清白白，从来没有做过对不起百姓的事。那个梦是假的，是您老人家想多了。随信还寄了一百两银子，说给爹买点好吃的，补补身体。
白世昌看了信，又看了银子，气得浑身发抖。他把银子摔在地上，把信撕得粉碎，指着南方骂：“逆子！逆子！”
白乙捡起银子，不敢说话。白世昌骂了半天，骂累了，躺在床上，闭上眼睛。他又做了一个梦。

Chapter 14 Dream Wolf
After Song Tao finished watching "Ghost Mother", he sat in front of the window for a long time. He missed that mother, her back as she walked through the wall, and her words of "I'm relieved." He thought of his mother, the look in her eyes before she died, and her words, "You have to live well." He thought for a long time, thinking about the moon rising and setting, before closing his eyes and falling asleep.
When he woke up the next day, he opened the Book of Heaven. The pages of the book turned by themselves and stopped on a blank page. He waited for the writing to appear.
This chapter is called "Dream Wolf".
There was an old man in Hebei, whose surname was Bai and whose name was Shichang. He served as county magistrate for a time. He returned to his hometown when he was old and spent his old age peacefully at home studying and educating his children. He has two sons, the eldest son Bai Jia and the second son Bai Yi. Bai Jia became an official and served as the magistrate of a county in the south of the Yangtze River; Bai Yi studied at home and served his father.
Bai Shichang hated corrupt officials most in his life. When he was the county magistrate, he was honest and self-responsible and never accepted bribes. When he left office, the people gave him a Wanmin umbrella, which he kept in the main hall like a treasure and burned incense every day. He often said to his two sons: "Being an official is like being a human being. You must be upright and pure. It is better to die poor than to die greedy."
After hearing this, Bai Jia agreed verbally but disagreed in his heart. He felt that his father was too pedantic, and he still talked like that despite his age. If you don't make money as an official, then what do you do as an official? After he took office, he was openly honest and fair, but secretly he was corrupt, perverting the law, accepting bribes, and taking human lives lightly. Whoever gives more money will be justified; whoever doesn't give money will be ignored. The people hated him to the core, but he was smart and managed well, and he remained firmly in his seat.
Bai Shichang didn't know this. He only saw that his son sent back more and more money every year. The letter said that the court had increased his salary, his superiors appreciated him, and the people loved him. Bai Shichang believed it to be true and praised everyone he met: "My son has a lot of potential and is much better than me."
This winter, Bai Shichang had a dream. In the dream, he was walking on a main road. As he was walking, he suddenly saw a group of people on the roadside, wearing rags and unkempt hair, being escorted forward by guards. Those people walked very slowly, one step at a time, as if their feet were shackled. Bai Shichang took a closer look and recognized several of them as people from his hometown, including neighbors, relatives, and his childhood playmates.
He was taken aback, grabbed a police officer and asked, "What crime have these people committed?"
The officer glanced at him and said, "They were all killed by your son."
Bai Shichang's face turned pale. "My son? Which son?"
"Baijia." The officer said, "He was an official in the south of the Yangtze River. He was corrupt and perverted the law, and preyed on the common people. These people were all the people under his rule. He forced them to live in exile here."
Bai Shichang was trembling all over, he couldn't believe it. He grabbed the guard and wanted to ask more questions, but the guard shook his hand away and said, "Go and see for yourself. His Yamen is in front of you."
Bai Shichang walked along the road and after walking for a while, he saw a government office. Two stone lions squatted at the entrance of the yamen, their mouths wide open, showing sharp teeth. As he was about to go in, a wolf suddenly jumped out of the door.
The wolf was gray and white, with blood-red eyes. It had a human hand in its mouth and was chewing it. When it saw Bai Shichang, it stopped and tilted its head to look at him. Bai Shichang was so frightened that his legs weakened and he took a few steps back. The wolf didn't pounce on him, but just stared at him for a long time, then turned around and walked slowly back to the Yamen.
Bai Shichang stood at the door and hesitated for a long time. He wanted to go in and have a look, but he was afraid of the wolf. Finally he took a step inside.
The yamen was gloomy, the light was dim, and there was blood everywhere on the ground. He walked forward along the corridor, walked to the lobby, opened the door, and saw a person sitting inside - no, not a human, a wolf. The wolf was wearing an official uniform and a black gauze hat. He was sitting on the chair of the Grand Master, with the case file in front of him, and he was reviewing the case. It holds a red pen in its paw and draws on the case file. Standing next to them were two wolf yamen servants, holding water and fire sticks in their hands and looking ferocious.
Bai Shichang looked at the wolf and suddenly felt that its features looked familiar. He took a closer look and was shocked - the wolf's features were exactly the same as his son Bai Jia.
"Jia'er?" His voice was trembling.
The wolf raised his head and glanced at him. Its eyes were red, but there was a hint of black in the red, a hint of white in the black, and a hint of white... something he couldn't recognize. That thing seemed like human nature, but also like ghost nature, like his son, but also like not.
"Dad," the wolf said, his voice exactly the same as Bai Jia's, "Why are you here?"
Bai Shichang's tears flowed down. He pointed at the wolf, his fingers trembling. "You...how did you become like this?"
Bai Jia looked down at his paws and smiled. The smile was the same as before, the corners of the mouth were curved, but the teeth exposed were pointed.
"Dad, that's what being an official is like. If you don't eat people, people will eat you. There's nothing I can do about it."
Bai Shichang was so angry that he was shaking all over. He pointed at Bai Jia's nose and cursed: "What did I teach you when you were a child? Be an upright person and be an official with integrity! Have you forgotten it?"
Bai Jia said nothing. It lowered its head, looked at the case files on the table, and was silent for a long time. Then it raised its head and looked at Bai Shichang. The redness in its eyes was lighter and darker.
"Dad, I remember everything you said. But I can't do it. In this world, an honest official cannot continue. If you are not greedy, others will be greedy; if you are honest, others will harm you. I don't want to harm others, but I don't want to be harmed by others."
Bai Shichang looked at it with pain and hatred in his heart. He thought of Bai Jia, who was fat and white when he was a child, and liked to lie on his lap and listen to stories. He told stories about Bao Gong, Hai Rui, and those upright officials. Bai Jia listened very carefully and said after listening: "Dad, when I grow up I also want to be an upright official." He smiled and said: "Okay, dad will wait."
He waited. What was waiting was a wolf.
He turned around and left. Get out of the yamen, get out of the road, get out of that dream. When he woke up, the pillow was wet and full of tears.
Bai Shichang is ill. He was lying on the bed, not eating or drinking, just in a daze. Bai Yi stayed in front of the bed and asked him what was wrong, but he didn't say anything. Asked if he felt uncomfortable, he shook his head. When I asked him what he was dreaming about, he burst into tears again.
Bai Yi panicked and hurriedly went to ask the doctor. The doctor came to see him and said that there was nothing serious wrong with the old man's health, but that he was suffering from a mental illness. Bai Yi asked what was wrong with him, and the doctor said he didn't know.
Bai Shichang lay down for three days. On the fourth day, he struggled to get up and asked Bai Yi to prepare paper and pen. Bai Yi brought it to him, and he wrote a letter to Bai Jia. The letter talked about that dream, saying that I dreamed that you turned into a wolf, saying that you were corrupt and perverting the law, preying on the common people. He said you should change quickly, return the money you were greedy for, and be a good person. If you don't change, I won't have a son like you.
Bai Yi sent the letter out. Two months later, Bai Jia's reply came. The letter was written very politely, saying, "Dad, don't worry, my son is innocent and has never done anything to offend the people." That dream is false, you, old man, are overthinking it. I also sent a hundred taels of silver with the letter, saying that I would buy some delicious food for my father to replenish his health.
Bai Shichang read the letter and then the money, trembling with anger. He threw the money on the ground, tore the letter into pieces, pointed at the south and cursed: "Treason! Treason!"
Bai Yi picked up the silver and didn't dare to speak. Bai Shichang cursed for a long time. When he was tired, he lay on the bed and closed his eyes. He had another dream.
